top_result_summaries.snippet: A **.gov** website belongs to an official government organization in the United States. # Investigation Update: Salmonella Outbreak, Cucumbers, November 2024. Epidemiologic and traceback data showed that cucumbers grown by Agrotato, S.A. de C.V. in Sonora, Mexico, were contaminated with *Salmonella* and made people sick. A total of 113 people infected with the outbreak strain of *Salmonella* were reported from 23 states. Illnesses started on dates ranging from October 12, 2024, to December 7, 2024. An illness sub-cluster is a group of unrelated sick people who all ate at the same location or event, such as a restaurant, long-term care facility, or school. Epidemiologic and traceback data show that cucumbers grown by Agrotato, S.A. de C.V. in Sonora, Mexico, including recalled cucumbers from SunFed Produce, LLC., may be contaminated with *Salmonella* and may be making people sick. As of December 17, 2024, a total of 100 people infected with the outbreak strain of *Salmonella* have been reported from 23 states.

top_result_summaries.title: Salmonella outbreak linked to backyard poultry grows to 104 illnesses, 1 death | CIDRAP
top_result_summaries.snippet: # Salmonella outbreak linked to backyard poultry grows to 104 illnesses, 1 death. A multistate *Salmonella* outbreak has grown in just a few weeks from 7 to 104 cases, with 1 death now recorded, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) said in an update yesterday. Since its previous update on May 5, the CDC has confirmed 97 new cases, and the number of affected states rose from 6 to 35. The death was in Illinois. "These outbreak strains have been linked to two hatcheries," the CDC said. The CDC in each of the past several years has reported large *Salmonella* outbreaks tied to backyard poultry. The 2024 outbreak included 470 confirmed cases and 1 death. Officials have confirmed chronic wasting disease (CWD) —an always-fatal prion disease that affects members of the deer family (cervids)—on a deer farm in Rock County, Wisconsin, according to a news release yesterday from the Wisconsin Department of Agriculture, Trade and Consumer Protection (DATCP).
